description:


title: `Request$otel` active binding is registered as `$otel_span`, silently returns `NULL`
description:
The active binding documented and consumed as `request$otel` is actually registered under the name `otel_span`. Because R6 environments don't do partial matching, `request$otel` returns `NULL`. This breaks OTel parent/child linking for every span created downstream (`routr`, `fiery`) and for reqres' own metric code.

In `R/request.R`:

```R
otel_span = function() {
  private$OPSAN
},
```

But every call uses `$otel`:

- In `reqres/R/otel.R`
- In `fiery/R/Fire.R`
- Even the [plumber2 OTel vignette](https://plumber2.posit.co/articles/otel.html) mentions it as `request$otel`

As a consequence, `routr` doesn't link subspans. Each `_route` span becomes a new root trace, making it impossible to see a request as a single trace in Tempo.

title: server.port is NA when Host header has no port
description:
In `R/otel.R`, three functions compute the OTel attribute `server.port` from the `Host` request header with the same regex:

```R
as.integer(sub("^.*:(.*)$", "\\1", request$host))
```

When the `Host` header contains no port, which is the default behind a revers proxy (Traefix in my case), the regex does not match anything, and returns `NA_integer_`. This NA then propagates to the OpenTelemetry attributes, with two different failures for traces and for metrics.

**For traces**, the server span is droped. The `otelsdk` package returns the following error:

```
Invalid argument: the entries of `attrs` must not contain missing (`NA`) values.
```

`otel::start_span()` catches the error, logs it to stderr, and returns a no-op span, so the request is missing from the trace pipeline.

**For metrics**, the `server.port` ends up as `-2147483648`.

## Reproducible example

I've tried to build a repex as well as possible, although it's not easy considering the bug only appears in production environment (behind a revers proxy).

Here is how to reproduce the error that eventually appears in `otelsdk`:

```R
Sys.setenv(
    OTEL_SERVICE_NAME = "reqres-reprex",
    OTEL_TRACES_EXPORTER  = "none",
    OTEL_LOGS_EXPORTER = "none",
    OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER = "none"
)
library(otelsdk)

host <- "api.example.com"
scheme <- "https"
server_port <- as.integer(sub("^.*:(.*)$", "\\1", host))

# A realistic span/metric attribute list, with the NA propagated from above:
attrs <- list(
    http.request.method = "GET",
    url.path = "/orders/42",
    url.scheme = scheme,
    network.protocol.name = "http",
    server.port = server_port,
    client.address = "10.0.0.5",
    server.address = host,
    user_agent.original = "curl/8.14.1"
)

# Failure in otelsdk
otelsdk:::as_otel_attributes(attrs)
```

## Expected behaviour

The attribute should capture the `server.port` as seen by the client and not `NA`.

According to [OpenTelemetry conventions](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/http/http-spans/#http-server), `server.address` and `server.port` are the original host and port as seen by the client. The spec gives an example with a reverse proxy in front of two hosts listening on 7070 and 8080, where `server.port` is reported as 443 because that is the TLS termination the client talked to.

To do this, instrumentations should derive `server.address` / `server.port` (and `url.scheme`) from the first of these that is available:

1. `Forwarded`
2. The `:authority` pseudo-header
3. The `Host` header

Also, when the source has no explicit port, it should fall back to the default port of the scheme (443 for https, 80 for http).

## Environment

- `reqres` 1.2.0 (CRAN)
- `otel` / `otelsdk` latest on CRAN
- R 4.4.3
- plumber2 behind Traefik

title: "error: missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed" -- request$get_header() parses dates wrong?
description:
hi.  in routr's `ressource_route()` function, there is a line
````
m_since <- request$get_header('If-Modified-Since')
````
it appears get_header returns a vector of length 2, the first being [day-name](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/If-Modified-Since#syntax), which is separated by a comma from the second element (day, month, year, ...).

when in the subsequent if statement, `m_since` is fed to `from_http_date()`, i'm guessing two `NAs` result.  which, it appears, results in the subject error message.

i took a quick look in the code in request.R, but didn't immediately see where the `headers` are set (maybe not even in reqres?  in fiery?  httpuv?).

a hack in routr would be something like
````
diff --git a/R/ressource_route.R b/R/ressource_route.R
index 02021fe..cb990a9 100644
--- a/R/ressource_route.R
+++ b/R/ressource_route.R
@@ -143,6 +143,10 @@ ressource_route <- function(..., default_file = 'index.html', default_ext = 'htm
       m_time <- file.mtime(real_file)
       etag <- request$get_header('If-None-Match')
       new_tag <- digest(m_time)
+      if (!is.null(m_since)) {
+          m_since <- paste(m_since, collapse=", ")
+      }
       if ((!is.null(m_since) && from_http_date(m_since) < m_time) ||
           (!is.null(etag) && etag == new_tag)) {
         response$status_with_text(304L)
````
cheers.

title: Add client interface to reqres
description:
Currently reqres is intended for server-side use. All the niceties realted to the `Request` and `Response` classes could be nice to have as a wrapper for `curl` calls as well.

Some considerations:
- Should it be tacket on to current classes or be a separat (sub)class?
    - If it should be tacked on there need to be a new constructor (this might come eventually if moving broader than rook). Also the read-only nature of the `Request` class needs to be reconsidered. Also, the 1-to-1 link of the `Request` and `Response` classes needs to be lifted somehow.
    - If put in separate (sub)class we might miss the possibility of doing manual redirection on the server
- The obvious interface will be a `send()` method in `Request` that performs a curl call, parses the response and creates a `Response` object

title: Parser for x-www-form-urlencoded appends newline to parameter value
description:
This code fragment parses a simulated `POST` request with one parameter. It appears that the parser is appending an unwanted newline (`\n`) to the parameter value.

```
fake_post <- fiery::fake_request(
  'http://example.com/test',
  method = "post",
  content = 'id=34632',
  headers = list(
    Content_Type = 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded'
  )
)

post_req <- Request$new(fake_post)
post_req$parse(`application/x-www-form-urlencoded` =
               parse_queryform() )
post_req$body
```

The output is:

```
$id
[1] "34632\n"
```

Notice that the `id` value has a trailing newline (`\n`), which seems wrong.

For a two parameters `POST`, the newline is appended to only the second parameter, not the first.
